doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Roomful of Blues near-miss, Scott's band and Widespread Depression
summary: He nearly joined Roomful of Blues, ended up in Scott Hamilton's band briefly, then went with Chuck Riggs to Widespread Depression in Vermont to save for New York.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: This would have been ‘75 I guess. So I went down to Providence and hung out on the scene with Hamilton a lot. Chris Flory had a quartet, because Scott already had his own band, with a great guitar player by the name of Fred Bates. And with Chuck Riggs as well, who followed him on into New York and everything. And we were sort of the two straight ahead or swing and bebop based jazz bands in Providence, so whatever gigs there were, you know Scott would get all the good ones and we’d sort of pick up the crumbs. But then they had a major personnel shift toward the end of my days in Providence, they had a big shake-up with Roomful of Blues with Duke Robillard on guitar, and Preston Hubbard, well actually that’s the story. I was living with Roomful’s baritone player, Doug Schlect, and there was all this rumbling in the band about personnel changes and stuff, and they wanted to get rid of their bass player and they wanted an upright and all this kind of stuff. So there was talk of me joining Roomful of Blues. So I got all the records that Duke told me to get, all the T-Bone Walker records and learned all the arrangements and stuff, for about a month. And then the big meeting happened and it turned out that they were going to take Preston Hubbard from Scott and then I would join Scott’s band, which I thought that’s much better anyway, I don’t have to play a bunch of blues all night long. I was already a swing and bopper by then. So that was a great thing but I think we only did six gigs before Scott left for New York and Chuck Riggs and I left for Widespread Depression up in Brattleboro, Vermont, where they were based at the time.
Can you explain that? Widespread Depression?

It’s the name of a swing and jump band that was based out of Marlboro College. Chuck Riggs and I spent six months there basically saving some money so we could move to New York. And that’s exactly what we did. And everyone in the band knew it. I remember the baritone player was being interviewed and he’s going, “Yeah, they’re using this band as a stepping stone.” © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -6-
